what_it_is.prose: Saab AB (Nasdaq Stockholm: SAAB-B) is a Swedish listed defence OEM headquartered in Stockholm. Saab's India footprint is anchored by the Carl-Gustaf M4 manufacturing facility in Haryana — the first 100% foreign direct investment (FDI) defence project cleared by the Indian government (November 2023). Saab FFV India Private Limited was incorporated as the Indian subsidiary; ground-breaking took place in March 2024 and production began in 2024. The Indian Army has operated the Carl-Gustaf recoilless rifle since 1976. In July 2026, the Indian Army issued a Request for Proposal (RFP) for 450 Carl-Gustaf M4 launchers, with deliveries required within 12 months and a 15-year product support plus 2-year warranty package. Saab also delivered the AT4 anti-armour weapon to the Indian Army under a January 2022 contract (per Janes; 'successfully delivered' confirmed per Saab Facebook). Saab's Gripen E fighter is a bidder for the Indian Air Force's 114 Multi-Role Combat Aircraft (MRCA) deal (estimated ₹3.25 lakh crore / €30 billion; Acceptance of Necessity cleared February 2026). IMPORTANT Atlas correction: The Atlas register references a '₹4,000 cr Aug 2024 deal' for Saab — this figure appears in 2023-era Facebook posts about Saab-OFB tie-up negotiations, but no primary source confirms the ₹4,000 crore figure or the August 2024 date. The M4 facility broke ground in March 2024 (not August 2024). The actual Saab FFV India investment value has not been disclosed in INR. The Polish $1.3 billion / SEK 12.9 billion Carl-Gustaf contract entered into force in June 2024 (not August 2024) — see REGISTER_TICKETS.md ticket P1-SAAB-4000CR-UNVERIFIED.

faq.question: Why is Saab's Carl-Gustaf M4 facility significant?
faq.answer: The Saab FFV India Private Limited Carl-Gustaf M4 manufacturing facility in Haryana is the first 100% foreign direct investment (FDI) defence project cleared by the Indian government (November 2023). It is the first foreign fully-owned defence production facility in India. Ground-breaking took place in March 2024 and production began in 2024. The facility produces the Carl-Gustaf M4 recoilless rifle for the Indian Army (which has operated the Carl-Gustaf since 1976) and for export to global Saab customers.

faq.question: Is the Atlas '₹4,000 cr Aug 2024 Saab deal' figure accurate?
faq.answer: No. The ₹4,000 crore figure appears in 2023-era Facebook posts about Saab-OFB tie-up negotiations, but no primary source confirms this specific figure or an August 2024 date. The M4 facility broke ground in March 2024 (not August 2024). The actual Saab FFV India investment value has not been disclosed in INR. The Polish $1.3 billion / SEK 12.9 billion Carl-Gustaf contract (a separate international order) entered into force in June 2024. See REGISTER_TICKETS.md ticket P1-SAAB-4000CR-UNVERIFIED.

faq.question: Is Saab bidding for the IAF's 114 MRCA deal?
faq.answer: Yes. Saab's Gripen E fighter is a bidder for the Indian Air Force's 114 Multi-Role Combat Aircraft (MRCA) deal, estimated at ₹3.25 lakh crore (€30 billion). The Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) was cleared in February 2026. The Gripen E competes against the Dassault Rafale, Boeing F/A-18EIn Super Hornet, Lockheed Martin F-21, Eurofighter Typhoon, and Sukhoi Su-35. The RfP has not yet been issued as of August 2026, and the bid outcome is pending.
